checks: Source 929f9f6bc9acea34 §3 (5)–(6) treats f=W_K−r on one supporting face. The frozen standalone identity allows a bounded step density and assumes an actual face path only when interpreting the profile term as a shape response.

Splitting at s=t and differentiating cancels both moving-boundary terms, giving C^1 regularity, zero endpoint values and −U''=f almost everywhere. Dividing the Green kernel by its positive peak gives the height-one tent.

The slope jumps are negative at c,d and add when c=d. The integration-by-parts boundary term is H(α)U'(α)−H(β)U'(β), giving the two trimming deductions exactly. The whole-face case has no endpoint terms.

The proposed compact nonnegative C^1 potential matches values and derivatives at x=h and x=2h and has positive left endpoint derivative. With support strictly left of c it makes the left trimming contribution strictly negative. The reflected construction handles right trimming. A nonnegative step supported on a positive portion of the roof gives the opposite sign.

Independently evaluated a rational trimmed example with left trim 1/8, c=1/2, h=1/10 and step values 6 and −2 on the two short support intervals. Direct integration and the signed formula both give −2/15.

overlap.comparison: Its cubic tight-triangle proof uses the same Green kernel after rescaling and gives unit-height ear costs for a particular signed measure with vanishing endpoint moments. The new formula retains nonzero endpoint derivatives and handles the actual signed roof with an inner base.
Its support-interpolation Green kernel is for −D²−1 in an angular variable. It does not evaluate the flat face tents and the signed trimming terms here.

readability: The one-half multiplier is conditional on a separately justified signed speed H/2. The calculus does not claim existence of such a body deformation.
